docs.title: The minimum valid page Beginner
docs.text:
Learn this skeleton by heart. Every page you build starts here.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My first page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Hello</h1>
</body>
</html>
Line Why it's there <!doctype html> Tells the browser to use standards mode. Without it you get "quirks mode", which emulates 1990s browser bugs. <html lang="en"> Root element. lang sets pronunciation for screen readers, hyphenation, spell-check and translation. <meta charset="utf-8"> Character encoding. Must be in the first 1024 bytes. Without it, characters like é or ₹ can turn into Ã©. <meta name="viewport" …> Makes mobile browsers use the device width instead of pretending to be 980px wide. Without it, responsive design doesn't work. <title> Shown in the browser tab, bookmarks and search results. Required.

docs.title: <!doctype html> Beginner
docs.text: Use: switches the browser into standards mode. Not an element, it's a declaration. Case-insensitive.

docs.title: <html> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: the root of the document. Everything else goes inside it.

Key attributes: lang (always set it), dir="rtl" for right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Hebrew.

docs.title: <head> Beginner
docs.text: Use: a container for metadata: things about the page, not shown in the page. Contains title, meta, link, style, script, base, noscript, template.

docs.title: <title> Beginner
docs.text:
<title>Pricing · Acme Cloud</title>

Use: the document's name. Put the specific part first ("Pricing") and the brand last, so tabs stay readable when they're narrow.

docs.title: <meta> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: metadata that has no dedicated element.

<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta name="description" content="Simple, predictable pricing for teams of any size.">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#e4572e">
<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow">

<!-- Open Graph: link previews in Slack, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, etc. -->
<meta property="og:title" content="Acme Cloud Pricing">
<meta property="og:description" content="Simple, predictable pricing.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.example/og.png">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://acme.example/pricing">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
name / property What it does viewport Mobile layout width. Never add user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1: they block zoom, which fails WCAG. description Snippet text in search results (~155 characters). theme-color Colours the browser UI on mobile. Accepts a media attribute for light/dark values. color-scheme Tells the browser your page supports dark mode, so form controls and scrollbars adapt before CSS loads. robots Search engine indexing rules. og:*, twitter:* Social preview cards.

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

http-equiv meta tags act like HTTP headers (Content-Security-Policy, refresh). Prefer real HTTP headers: they apply before parsing and some directives (like CSP's frame-ancestors) are ignored in meta form.

docs.title: <link> Beginner → Advanced
docs.text:
Use: connects the page to external resources.

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/main.css">
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
<link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.example/pricing">

<!-- Performance hints -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="/hero.avif" as="image" fetchpriority="high">
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/js/app.js">
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://cdn.example.com">

<!-- Print-only stylesheet -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/print.css" media="print">
rel Use stylesheet Load CSS. Blocks rendering until loaded (that's on purpose). icon Favicon. SVG favicons can include a prefers-color-scheme media query. manifest Web app manifest for installable PWAs. canonical The preferred URL for duplicate content (SEO). preconnect Open a connection to another origin early. Use for 1–3 critical origins only. preload Fetch a resource you will need on this page, now, with high priority. modulepreload Preload a JS module and its parse. prefetch Fetch a resource the next page might need, at low priority. alternate Alternate versions: hreflang translations, RSS feeds.

docs.title: <style> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: CSS inside the HTML document.

<style>
  body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
</style>

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

Inlining the critical CSS (what's needed for the first screen) in a <style> tag and loading the rest async can noticeably improve LCP. Don't inline everything; you lose browser caching across pages.

docs.title: <script> Beginner → Advanced
docs.text:
Use: runs JavaScript, or holds data (type="application/ld+json", type="importmap").

<!-- Classic script: blocks HTML parsing while it downloads and runs -->
<script src="legacy.js"></script>

<!-- defer: download in parallel, run in order after HTML is parsed -->
<script src="app.js" defer></script>

<!-- async: download in parallel, run as soon as it arrives (any order) -->
<script src="analytics.js" async></script>

<!-- module: deferred by default, strict mode, supports import/export -->
<script type="module" src="main.js"></script>

<!-- import map: name bare imports -->
<script type="importmap">
  { "imports": { "lit": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lit@3/+esm" } }
</script>

<!-- Structured data for search engines -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
  { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Organization", "name": "Acme" }
</script>

gantt
    dateFormat X
    axisFormat %s
    section Plain script
    Parse HTML  :0, 3
    Download    :3, 5
    Execute     :5, 6
    Parse rest  :6, 9
    section defer
    Parse HTML  :0, 9
    Download    :1, 4
    Execute     :9, 10
    section async
    Parse HTML  :0, 4
    Download    :1, 4
    Execute     :4, 5
    Parse rest  :5, 9

Rule of thumb: use type="module" or defer for your app code. Use async only for independent scripts like analytics.

docs.title: <noscript> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: content shown only when JavaScript is disabled.

<noscript>
  <p>This app needs JavaScript. Here's a <a href="/basic">basic version</a>.</p>
</noscript>

docs.title: <base> Advanced
docs.text:
Use: sets the base URL for every relative URL in the document. Only one per page.

<base href="https://docs.example.com/v2/">

Warning

<base> also changes where #anchor links point. <a href="#top"> becomes https://docs.example.com/v2/#top, which can break in-page navigation. Avoid it unless you need it.

docs.title: <body> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: contains everything visible on the page. One per document.

Senior note · 🔴 Expert

The browser builds the DOM top to bottom. Stylesheets in <head> block rendering; scripts without defer/async block parsing. A good <head> order: charset → viewport → title → preconnect → critical CSS → preload → stylesheets → deferred scripts → SEO and social meta. Tools like capo.js check this ordering for you.

docs.title: Forms & Inputs
docs.text: Forms are where most accessibility bugs live and where native HTML saves you the most code. Built-in elements give you keyboard support, mobile keyboards, validation and autofill for free.

docs.title: <form> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: collects user input and sends it to a server.

<form action="/signup" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
</form>
Email Sign up Attribute Use action URL to send the data to (defaults to the current URL) method get (data in the URL; use for search/filter) or post (data in the body; use for changes) enctype multipart/form-data is required for file uploads novalidate Turn off built-in validation (you'll do it in JS) autocomplete on / off for the whole form

The name attribute on each control is what gets submitted. No name, no data.

docs.title: <label> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: the visible, clickable name of a control. Clicking the label focuses or toggles the input, which makes small checkboxes much easier to hit.

<!-- Explicit: for + id -->
<label for="name">Full name</label>
<input id="name" name="name">

<!-- Implicit: wrap the input -->
<label><input type="checkbox" name="terms"> I accept the terms</label>
Full name I accept the terms

Placeholder is not a label

Placeholder text disappears when the user types, is usually low-contrast, and isn't reliably announced. Every input needs a real <label>.

docs.title: <input>: all 22 types Beginner
docs.text: Each type gives a different control, a different mobile keyboard and different built-in validation. Try them in the Output boxes.

docs.title: Text-like inputs
docs.text:
<label>text     <input type="text" placeholder="Any text"></label>
<label>email    <input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com"></label>
<label>password <input type="password" value="secret123"></label>
<label>search   <input type="search" placeholder="Search…"></label>
<label>tel      <input type="tel" placeholder="+91 98765 43210"></label>
<label>url      <input type="url" placeholder="https://"></label>
<label>number   <input type="number" min="0" max="10" step="1" value="3"></label>
text email password search tel url number Type Mobile keyboard Built-in validation text Standard none email Has @ and . Must look like an email; multiple allows a comma list password Standard, masked none search "Search"/"Go" key; may show a clear ✕ none tel Phone keypad none (phone formats vary; use pattern) url Has / and .com Must be an absolute URL number Numeric min, max, step

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

Don't use type="number" for things that are digits but not quantities (OTP codes, card numbers, PIN codes, ZIP codes). Spinners and scroll-wheel changes make no sense there, and leading zeros are lost. Use type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code" instead.

docs.title: Date and time inputs
docs.text:
<input type="date">
<input type="time">
<input type="datetime-local">
<input type="month">
<input type="week">
date time datetime-local month week

The value is always submitted in ISO format (2026-10-19) regardless of how it's displayed. month and week aren't supported in Firefox/Safari desktop; they fall back to a text field.

docs.title: Choice inputs
docs.text:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m" checked> Medium</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="l"> Large</label>
</fieldset>

<label><input type="checkbox" checked> Gift wrap</label>
<label><input type="checkbox" switch> Notifications</label>  <!-- Safari 17.4+ switch -->
Size Small Medium Large

Gift wrap Notifications

  • Radio: pick exactly one. All radios in a group share the same name. Arrow keys move between them.
  • Checkbox: on/off, independently. Can be set to indeterminate via JS (the "some selected" state).

docs.title: Other inputs
docs.text:
<input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="60">
<input type="color" value="#e4572e">
<input type="file" accept="image/*" multiple>
<input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="abc123">
<input type="image" src="go.png" alt="Go">
<input type="submit" value="Submit">
<input type="reset" value="Reset">
<input type="button" value="Plain button">
range color file hidden(nothing visible, still submitted) image submit / reset / button

<input type=submit> vs <button>

Prefer <button>: it can contain HTML (icons, <span>s), while <input> buttons only take a value string.

docs.title: Validation attributes Beginner
docs.text:
<input required>
<input minlength="3" maxlength="20">
<input type="number" min="1" max="99" step="1">
<input pattern="[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}" title="Format: ABC-1234">
Order code Check

Try submitting with an empty or wrongly formatted value: the browser shows its own error bubble.

Style validation state with CSS. :user-invalid only matches after the user has interacted, so fields don't show red before anyone types:

input:user-invalid { border-color: crimson; }
input:user-valid   { border-color: seagreen; }

docs.title: autocomplete, inputmode, enterkeyhint Intermediate
docs.text:
<input name="name"   autocomplete="name">
<input name="email"  autocomplete="email" type="email">
<input name="phone"  autocomplete="tel" type="tel">
<input name="addr"   autocomplete="street-address">
<input name="pin"    autocomplete="postal-code" inputmode="numeric">
<input name="cc"     autocomplete="cc-number" inputmode="numeric">
<input name="otp"    autocomplete="one-time-code" inputmode="numeric">
<input name="new-pw" autocomplete="new-password" type="password">
<input name="q"      enterkeyhint="search" type="search">
  • autocomplete tokens let browsers and password managers fill fields correctly. It's also a WCAG 2.2 requirement (1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose).
  • inputmode picks the on-screen keyboard: none, text, decimal, numeric, tel, search, email, url.
  • enterkeyhint changes the label on the mobile Enter key: enter, done, go, next, previous, search, send.

docs.title: <button> Beginner
docs.text:
<button type="submit">Submit (default in a form)</button>
<button type="button">Plain action</button>
<button type="reset">Reset form</button>
<button type="button" disabled>Disabled</button>

docs.title: <select>, <option>, <optgroup> Beginner
docs.text:
<label for="city">City</label>
<select id="city" name="city">
  <option value="">Choose a city</option>
  <optgroup label="India">
    <option value="blr" selected>Bengaluru</option>
    <option value="mum">Mumbai</option>
  </optgroup>

</select>

New: customizable <select> · 🟠 Advanced

Chromium 135+ supports fully styleable selects with select, ::picker(select) { appearance: base-select; }, including rich HTML inside <option>. Other browsers ignore it and show the normal select, so it's safe progressive enhancement.

docs.title: <datalist> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: suggestions for a text input. Unlike <select>, users can still type anything.

<label for="browser">Browser</label>
<input id="browser" list="browsers">
<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Chrome"></option>
  <option value="Firefox"></option>
  <option value="Safari"></option>
  <option value="Edge"></option>
</datalist>
Browser

docs.title: <textarea> Beginner
docs.text:
<label for="msg">Message</label>
<textarea id="msg" name="msg" rows="4" cols="40" maxlength="500"></textarea>
Message

The demo uses field-sizing: content (Chromium 123+): the textarea grows as you type, with no JavaScript.

docs.title: <fieldset> and <legend> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: group related controls with a caption. Required for radio groups so screen readers announce the question ("Size, radio group"). <fieldset disabled> disables everything inside.

<fieldset>
  <legend>Shipping address</legend>
  <label>Street <input name="street"></label>
  <label>City <input name="city"></label>
</fieldset>
Shipping address Street City

docs.title: <output> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: the result of a calculation or user action. Screen readers announce changes to it.

<form oninput="total.value = Number(a.value) * Number(b.value)">
  <input name="a" type="number" value="4"> ×
  <input name="b" type="number" value="5"> =
  <output name="total" for="a b">20</output>
</form>
× = 20

docs.title: <progress> and <meter> Beginner
docs.text:
• <progress>: how far a task has got. No value = indeterminate (spinning).
  • <meter>: a measurement within a known range (disk usage, password strength). Turns yellow/red past low/high.
<label>Upload <progress value="70" max="100">70%</progress></label>
<label>Loading <progress></progress></label>

<label>Disk <meter value="0.3" low="0.6" high="0.85" optimum="0.1">30%</meter></label>
<label>Disk <meter value="0.7" low="0.6" high="0.85" optimum="0.1">70%</meter></label>
<label>Disk <meter value="0.95" low="0.6" high="0.85" optimum="0.1">95%</meter></label>

Upload 70% Loading

Disk 30% Disk 70% Disk 95%

Senior note · 🔴 Expert

Form UX checklist for design reviews: one column; labels above inputs; mark optional fields rather than required ones when most are required; inline errors linked with aria-describedby; error summary at the top on submit, with focus moved to it; never clear user input on error; autocomplete on every personal-data field; minimum 24×24 CSS px targets (WCAG 2.5.8); don't disable the submit button (explain what's wrong instead).

docs.title: Global Attributes
docs.text: Global attributes work on every HTML element.

docs.title: Core Beginner
docs.text: Attribute Use Example id Unique identifier on the page. Targets for links (#id), labels (for), ARIA and JS. <section id="pricing"> class Space-separated names for CSS and JS. Reusable. <div class="card card--featured"> style Inline CSS. Highest specificity in author styles; avoid except for dynamic values. <div style="--progress: 40%"> title Advisory tooltip. Not accessible on touch or keyboard; don't rely on it. <abbr title="…"> lang Language of the content. <p lang="hi">नमस्ते</p> dir Text direction: ltr, rtl, auto. <p dir="auto"> hidden Hides the element (like display:none). <div hidden>

docs.title: hidden and hidden="until-found" Intermediate
docs.text:
<p hidden>You can't see me.</p>
<div hidden="until-found">Browser find-in-page (Ctrl+F) can reveal me.</div>

until-found (Chromium 102+; Firefox and Safari recently) keeps content findable and indexable while collapsed, which is perfect for accordions. The beforematch event fires before it's revealed.

docs.title: data-* custom data Beginner
docs.text:
<button data-product-id="4821" data-variant="blue">Add to cart</button>

<script>
  btn.dataset.productId;   // "4821" (kebab-case → camelCase)
</script>

<style>
  [data-variant="blue"] { background: royalblue; color: white; }
</style>
Add to cart

docs.title: Interaction Intermediate
docs.text:
Attribute Use tabindex="0" Make a non-focusable element focusable, in DOM order. tabindex="-1" Focusable by script (el.focus()) but not by Tab. Used for headings you move focus to. tabindex="1+" ❌ Never: it breaks the natural focus order. autofocus Focus on page load / dialog open. Use sparingly. accesskey Keyboard shortcut. Conflicts with assistive tech shortcuts, so rarely recommended. contenteditable Makes content editable: true, false, plaintext-only. draggable true to allow native drag and drop. spellcheck true / false inputmode, enterkeyhint Virtual keyboard hints (also work on contenteditable). autocapitalize off, sentences, words, characters 
<p contenteditable="true">Click and edit this text.</p>

Click and edit this text.

docs.title: inert Intermediate Baseline 2023
docs.text:
Use: makes an element and its whole subtree non-interactive: no focus, no clicks, hidden from assistive tech. Use it on the page behind an off-canvas menu or a custom modal.

docs.title: Accessibility: role and aria-* Advanced
docs.text:
ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) changes what assistive technology announces. It doesn't change behaviour: role="button" won't make a <div> keyboard-operable.

The five rules of ARIA:

  1. If a native HTML element does the job, use it instead of ARIA.
  2. Don't change native semantics (<h2 role="tab"> ❌) unless you really must.
  3. All interactive ARIA controls must be keyboard operable.
  4. Don't use role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true" on a focusable element.
  5. All interactive elements must have an accessible name.
Attribute Use aria-label Accessible name when there's no visible text: <button aria-label="Close">✕</button> aria-labelledby Name from another element's text (by id) aria-describedby Extra description: hint or error text aria-expanded true/false on a button that toggles something aria-controls id of the element the control affects aria-current page, step, date… marks the current item in a set aria-live polite / assertive: announce dynamic updates (toasts, results counts) aria-hidden="true" Hide decorative content from assistive tech aria-invalid Mark a field as invalid aria-busy Region is updating aria-pressed Toggle buttons (true / false / mixed) 
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="filters">Filters</button>
<div id="filters" hidden>…</div>

<label for="pw">Password</label>
<input id="pw" type="password" aria-describedby="pw-hint pw-err" aria-invalid="true">
<p id="pw-hint">At least 12 characters.</p>
<p id="pw-err">Too short.</p>

<p aria-live="polite" id="status">3 results</p>

docs.title: <a> Anchor (link) Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a hyperlink to another page, a file, a section of the same page, an email address or a phone number.

<p>
  <a href="/about">Internal link</a> ·
  <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org" target="_blank" rel="noopener">External, new tab</a> ·
  <a href="#forms">Jump to a section</a> ·
  <a href="mailto:hi@example.com">Email us</a> ·
  <a href="tel:+911234567890">Call us</a> ·
  <a href="/report.pdf" download>Download PDF</a>
</p>

Internal link · External, new tab · Jump to a section · Email us · Call us · Download PDF

Key attributes: href, target, rel (noopener, noreferrer, nofollow, sponsored, ugc), download, hreflang, referrerpolicy.

Link or button?

Links go somewhere (change the URL). Buttons do something (submit, open, toggle). Never use <a href="#" onclick="…"> for an action, and never put a <button> inside an <a>.

Senior note · 🟡 Intermediate

Modern browsers apply rel="noopener" to target="_blank" automatically, but writing it is still good practice for older browsers. Link text must make sense out of context: "Read the pricing guide", not "Click here".

docs.title: Interactive Elements & Web Components
docs.text: Modern HTML can do things that used to need a JavaScript library: accordions, modals, menus and tooltips. Native versions handle focus, keyboard and screen readers for you.

</details>

<details open>

docs.title: Exclusive accordion with name Intermediate Baseline 2024
docs.text:
Give several <details> the same name and only one can be open at a time.

<details name="faq" open><summary>Shipping</summary><p>3–5 days.</p></details>
<details name="faq"><summary>Returns</summary><p>30 days, free.</p></details>
<details name="faq"><summary>Warranty</summary><p>2 years.</p></details>
Shipping

3–5 days.

Returns

30 days, free.

Warranty

2 years.

Style the marker:

summary { list-style: none; cursor: pointer; }           /* hide the triangle */
summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }      /* older Safari */
summary::after { content: "+"; float: inline-end; }
details[open] > summary::after { content: "−"; }

/* Animate open/close height (Chromium 131+) */
details::details-content {
  block-size: 0; overflow: hidden;
  transition: block-size .3s, content-visibility .3s allow-discrete;
}
details[open]::details-content { block-size: auto; }
:root { interpolate-size: allow-keywords; }  /* lets 'auto' animate */

docs.title: <dialog> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: a modal or non-modal dialog. showModal() gives you, for free: a backdrop, focus moved inside, the rest of the page made inert, Esc to close, and rendering on the top layer above every z-index.

<button type="button" onclick="dlg.showModal()">Delete project…</button>

<dialog id="dlg" aria-labelledby="dlg-title">
  <h2 id="dlg-title">Delete project?</h2>
  <p>This can't be undone.</p>
  <form method="dialog">
    <button value="cancel">Cancel</button>
    <button value="delete">Delete</button>
  </form>
</dialog>

dialog::backdrop { background: rgb(0 0 0 / .5); backdrop-filter: blur(2px); }
Delete project…
  • <form method="dialog"> closes the dialog on submit and sets dialog.returnValue to the clicked button's value.
  • show() opens it non-modally (no backdrop, page still interactive).
  • New: closedby="any" (Chromium 134+) lets a click on the backdrop close it.

docs.text:
Use: menus, tooltips, toasts and pickers that float on the top layer. Declarative: no JS needed to open and close.

<button popovertarget="menu">Open menu</button>

<div id="menu" popover>
  <a href="#">Profile</a>
  <a href="#">Settings</a>
  <a href="#">Sign out</a>
</div>
Open menu

Profile

Settings

Sign out

Feature popover (auto) popover="manual" popover="hint" Closes on outside click / Esc ✅ ❌ (you close it) ✅ Closes other auto popovers ✅ ❌ ❌ (closes other hints) Typical use Menus, pickers Toasts Tooltips

popovertargetaction="show | hide | toggle" controls what the button does. Pair popovers with CSS anchor positioning to attach them to their button.

dialog vs popover

Use <dialog> + showModal() when the user must respond before continuing (blocks the page). Use popover for lightweight, dismissable UI that doesn't block anything.

docs.title: <template> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: inert HTML that isn't rendered, ready to be cloned by JavaScript.

<ul id="list"></ul>

<template id="row">
  <li><strong class="name"></strong> — <span class="role"></span></li>
</template>

<script>
  const tpl = document.getElementById('row');
  for (const [name, role] of [['Asha', 'Design'], ['Ravi', 'Frontend']]) {
    const li = tpl.content.cloneNode(true);
    li.querySelector('.name').textContent = name;
    li.querySelector('.role').textContent = role;
    document.getElementById('list').append(li);
  }
</script>

docs.title: Custom elements, Shadow DOM and <slot> Advanced
docs.text:
Use: build your own reusable HTML tags (Web Components) with encapsulated styles. They work in any framework or none.

<user-card>
  <span slot="name">Asha Rao</span>
  <span slot="role">Design Lead</span>
</user-card>

<script>
  customElements.define('user-card', class extends HTMLElement {
    constructor() {
      super();
      this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' }).innerHTML = `
        <style>
          :host { display: inline-block; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 12px;
                  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #e4572e, #f3a712); color: white; }
          ::slotted([slot=role]) { opacity: .85; font-size: .9em; }
        </style>
        <strong><slot name="name">Anonymous</slot></strong><br>
        <slot name="role"></slot>`;
    }
  });
</script>
Asha RaoDesign Lead
  • Custom element names must contain a hyphen (user-card).
  • <slot> is where the light-DOM children get projected. Named slots match slot="…".
  • Styles inside the shadow root don't leak out; page styles don't leak in (except inherited properties like color and font, and ::part()).

docs.title: Declarative Shadow DOM Expert Baseline 2024
docs.text:
Server-render a shadow root without JavaScript:

<user-card>
  <template shadowrootmode="open">
    <style>:host { display:block; border:1px solid #ccc; padding:1rem; }</style>
    <slot></slot>
  </template>
  Rendered on the server, encapsulated, no JS required.
</user-card>

Senior note · 🔴 Expert

Web Components shine for design systems shared across frameworks (React, Angular, Vue, plain pages). Trade-offs: SSR needs declarative shadow DOM; form participation needs ElementInternals; ARIA references (aria-labelledby) can't cross shadow boundaries yet; and global CSS such as a reset doesn't reach inside the shadow root. Many teams use Lit to cut the boilerplate.

docs.title: <img> Image Beginner → Advanced
docs.text:
Use: embed an image.

<img src="https://picsum.photos/id/1015/320/180"
     alt="A river winding through a green valley"
     width="320" height="180"
     loading="lazy" decoding="async">
Attribute Why src Image URL (required) alt Text alternative (required). Describe the purpose. For purely decorative images use alt="" so screen readers skip them. width / height Intrinsic size. The browser reserves space before the image loads, which prevents layout shift (CLS). Always set them, then let CSS make the image responsive. loading="lazy" Don't load until it's near the viewport. Never lazy-load the hero / LCP image. decoding="async" Decode off the main thread. fetchpriority="high" Boost the LCP image's priority. srcset / sizes Responsive image candidates (below). 
/* The responsive image rule everyone uses */
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }

docs.title: Writing good alt text
docs.text: Image Good alt Product photo in a shop alt="Blue Cloud Runner shoe, side view" Logo that links home alt="Acme home" (describe the link's purpose) Chart Short summary in alt, full data in a table or caption Decorative swirl alt="" Icon next to the text "Delete" alt="" (the text already says it)

docs.title: Responsive images with srcset and sizes Intermediate
docs.text:
<!-- Resolution switching: same image, different file sizes -->
<img
  src="photo-800.jpg"
  srcset="photo-400.jpg 400w, photo-800.jpg 800w, photo-1600.jpg 1600w"
  sizes="(min-width: 1024px) 50vw, 100vw"
  alt="…" width="800" height="533">

Read it as: "This image shows at 50% of the viewport on screens ≥ 1024px, otherwise full width. Here are three files and their real widths; browser, pick the smallest one that's sharp enough for this screen's pixel density."

docs.title: <picture> and <source> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: offer different formats (AVIF → WebP → JPEG) or different crops at different screen sizes (art direction).

<picture>
  <!-- Art direction: square crop on phones -->
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="hero-square.avif" type="image/avif">
  <!-- Modern formats first, browser picks the first it supports -->
  <source srcset="hero.avif" type="image/avif">
  <source srcset="hero.webp" type="image/webp">
  <!-- Fallback + where alt, width, height live -->
  <img src="hero.jpg" alt="Team working together" width="1200" height="600">
</picture>

The <img> inside is required: it's what actually renders. <source> only swaps its src.

Browsers only allow it with muted. muted, loop Self-explanatory playsinline Play inside the page on iOS instead of going fullscreen poster Image shown before playback preload none, metadata (recommended), auto

docs.title: <iframe> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: embed another web page: maps, YouTube, payment widgets.

<iframe
  src="https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html?bbox=77.58,12.96,77.62,12.99"
  title="Map of central Bengaluru"
  width="100%" height="220"
  loading="lazy"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
  sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"></iframe>

Always set a title (screen readers announce it). Use sandbox to restrict what embedded third-party content can do, and allow="…" to grant specific permissions (camera, fullscreen).

docs.title: <embed> and <object> Advanced
docs.text:
Legacy ways to embed plugins (Flash, Java applets). Today their main remaining use is embedding PDFs, where <iframe> works just as well. Prefer <iframe>, <video> or <img>.

<object data="guide.pdf" type="application/pdf" width="100%" height="400">
  <a href="guide.pdf">Download the guide (PDF)</a>
</object>

docs.title: <svg> Inline SVG Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: vector graphics that are crisp at any size and can be styled with CSS. Ideal for icons, logos and charts.

<svg width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 120 120" role="img" aria-label="Orange circle with a check mark">
  <circle cx="60" cy="60" r="54" fill="#e4572e"/>
  <path d="M35 62 l17 17 l33 -36" fill="none" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="10"
        stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
</svg>

Icons

Use fill="currentColor" in icon SVGs so they inherit the text colour, and they'll follow hover states and dark mode automatically. Decorative icons get aria-hidden="true".

docs.title: <canvas> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: a pixel drawing surface for JavaScript: games, charts with thousands of points, image editing. Not accessible on its own, so provide fallback content or an alternative.

<canvas id="c" width="240" height="100">A red-to-blue gradient bar.</canvas>
<script>
  const ctx = document.getElementById('c').getContext('2d');
  const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 240, 0);
  g.addColorStop(0, '#e4572e');
  g.addColorStop(1, '#3f51b5');
  ctx.fillStyle = g;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 20, 240, 60);
</script>
A red-to-blue gradient bar.

docs.title: <map> and <area> Advanced
docs.text:
Use: clickable regions on an image (image maps). Rare today; an inline SVG with <a> elements is usually easier to make responsive.

<img src="floor.png" alt="Office floor plan" usemap="#floor" width="400" height="200">
<map name="floor">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,200,200" href="/rooms/a" alt="Meeting room A">
  <area shape="circle" coords="300,100,60" href="/rooms/b" alt="Lounge">
</map>

docs.title: Sectioning & Landmarks
docs.text: Sectioning elements describe the regions of a page. Screen readers expose them as landmarks, so users can jump straight to the navigation, the main content or the search box. They also give you meaningful CSS hooks instead of div.header.

docs.title: The page skeleton Beginner
docs.text:
<body>
  <a class="skip-link" href="#content">Skip to content</a>
  <header>
    <a href="/">Logo</a>
    <nav aria-label="Primary">…</nav>
    <search>…</search>
  </header>

  <main id="content">
    <article>
      <h1>Article title</h1>
      <section>
        <h2>Part one</h2>
        …
      </section>
    </article>
    <aside>Related links</aside>
  </main>

  <footer>© 2026 Acme</footer>
</body>
<header> logo · <nav> · <search> <main> <article> h1 <section> h2 <section> h2 <aside> <footer> Element Landmark role When it's a landmark <header> banner Only when it's a direct child of <body> (not inside article/section/main) <nav> navigation Always <main> main Always <aside> complementary At top level, or with an accessible name <footer> contentinfo Only when it's a direct child of <body> <section> region Only when it has an accessible name (aria-labelledby / aria-label) <search> search Always <form> form Only when it has an accessible name <article> article Always (not a landmark, but a document structure role)

docs.title: <header> BeginnerWhy Grid beats floats
docs.text:
Use: introductory content for the page or for a section: logo, title, nav, author info. A page can have several (one per article).

<article>
  <header>
    <h2>Why Grid beats floats</h2>
    <p>By Asha · <time datetime="2026-10-01">1 Oct 2026</time></p>
  </header>
  <p>…</p>
</article>

By Asha · 1 Oct 2026

…

docs.title: <nav> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a block of major navigation links: main menu, breadcrumbs, table of contents, pagination. Not every group of links needs <nav> (footer legal links usually don't).

<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/docs">Docs</a></li>
    <li><a aria-current="page">Flexbox</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
  1. Home /
  2. Docs /
  3. Flexbox

Senior note · 🟡 Intermediate

With more than one <nav> on a page, give each an aria-label ("Primary", "Breadcrumb", "Pagination") so screen reader users can tell them apart. Use aria-current="page" on the link to the current page.

docs.title: <main> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: the dominant content of the page. Exactly one visible <main> per page. Not inside article, aside, header, footer or nav.

<a class="skip-link" href="#content">Skip to content</a>
<main id="content">…</main>

The skip link lets keyboard users jump past a long header. Hide it until it gets focus:

.skip-link { position: absolute; translate: 0 -200%; }
.skip-link:focus { translate: 0 0; }

docs.title: <article> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: self-contained content that makes sense on its own and could be syndicated: a blog post, a news story, a product card, a forum comment.

Test: "Would this still make sense in an RSS feed?" If yes, it's an <article>.

<article class="product">
  <img src="shoe.jpg" alt="Blue running shoe" width="120" height="80">
  <h3>Cloud Runner</h3>
  <p>₹4,999</p>
</article>

docs.title: <section> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a thematic grouping of content, with a heading. If you can't think of a heading for it, it's probably a <div>.

<section aria-labelledby="pricing-h">
  <h2 id="pricing-h">Pricing</h2>
  …
</section>

section vs article vs div

  • article: stands alone (a card, a post).
  • section: a chapter of something bigger, with a heading.
  • div: no meaning, styling only.

docs.title: <aside> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: content related to the surrounding content, but separate from it: sidebars, pull quotes, "related articles", ads.

<aside>
  <h3>Did you know?</h3>
  <p>Flexbox shipped in all major browsers in 2015.</p>
</aside>
Did you know?

Flexbox shipped in all major browsers in 2015.

docs.title: <footer> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: footer for the page or a section: copyright, author, related links, contact.

<footer>
  <p>© 2026 Acme Inc. · <a href="/privacy">Privacy</a></p>
</footer>

docs.title: <address> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: contact information for the nearest <article> or the whole page. Not for any postal address in the text.

<address>
  Written by <a href="mailto:asha@example.com">Asha</a>.<br>
  Acme Inc., Bengaluru
</address>
Written by Asha. Acme Inc., Bengaluru

docs.title: <hgroup> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: a heading grouped with a subtitle or tagline. Since 2023 the spec allows one heading plus <p> elements.

<hgroup>
  <h1>Web UI Frontend Playbook</h1>
  <p>From your first tag to frontend architect.</p>
</hgroup>
Web UI Frontend Playbook

From your first tag to frontend architect.

docs.title: <search> Intermediate new 2023
docs.text:
Use: wraps search or filter controls. It's the native version of <div role="search">. Baseline since 2023.

<search>
  <form action="/search">
    <label for="q">Search docs</label>
    <input id="q" name="q" type="search" placeholder="e.g. flexbox">
    <button>Search</button>
  </form>
</search>
Search docs Search

Senior note · 🔴 Expert

The "document outline algorithm" never shipped. HTML5 once proposed that <h1> inside a nested <section> would be treated as an <h2>. No browser or screen reader implemented it and it was removed from the spec in 2022. Always use explicit heading levels (h1–h6) that match the real nesting depth. Also, browsers are removing the default smaller font-size for h1 inside article/section, so set heading sizes explicitly in CSS.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: Use tables for tabular data only: things with rows and columns that relate to each other (prices, schedules, comparisons). Never use tables for page layout; that's what Flexbox and Grid are for.

docs.title: Every table element
docs.text: Element Use <table> The table container <caption> The table's title. First child of <table>. Screen readers announce it. <colgroup> / <col> Style whole columns. Only background, border, width and visibility work on columns. <thead> Header rows. Repeats on each printed page. <tbody> Body rows. A table can have several, to group rows. <tfoot> Summary rows (totals) <tr> A table row <th> A header cell. scope="col" or scope="row" tells assistive tech what it labels. <td> A data cell

docs.title: Spanning cells Beginner
docs.text:
<table>
  <tr><th rowspan="2">Mon</th><td>9:00 Standup</td></tr>
  <tr><td>14:00 Design review</td></tr>
  <tr><th>Tue</th><td>10:00 Planning</td></tr>
</table>
Mon9:00 Standup 14:00 Design review Tue10:00 Planning

colspan="n" merges cells across columns; rowspan="n" merges down rows.

docs.title: Styling tables Intermediate
docs.text:
table {
  border-collapse: collapse;       /* single borders instead of doubled */
  inline-size: 100%;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;   /* digits line up in columns */
}
th, td {
  padding: .5rem .75rem;
  border-block-end: 1px solid #ddd;
  text-align: start;
}
td:is(:nth-child(n+2)) { text-align: end; }  /* right-align numbers */
tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f6f7f9; }   /* zebra stripes */
tbody tr:hover { background: #fff1ea; }
thead th { position: sticky; inset-block-start: 0; background: white; }  /* sticky header */

docs.title: Responsive tables Intermediate
docs.text:
Tables don't shrink well. Two reliable patterns:

1. Horizontal scroll (simplest)2. Stack cells as cards on small screens 
<div class="table-scroll" role="region" aria-labelledby="cap" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="cap">Quarterly results</caption>
    …
  </table>
</div>

.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto; }

tabindex="0" makes the scroll area keyboard-scrollable; role="region" + label makes it announceable.

<td data-label="Storage">100 GB</td>

@media (max-width: 600px) {
  thead { display: none; }
  tr, td { display: block; }
  td::before { content: attr(data-label) ": "; font-weight: 700; }
}

Warning

Changing display on table elements can strip their table semantics in some browsers. Add role="table", role="row", role="cell" explicitly if you use this pattern.

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

For complex tables with multi-level headers, use id on each <th> and headers="id1 id2" on each <td>. Test with a screen reader in table mode (Ctrl+Alt+Right in VoiceOver/NVDA) to hear what each cell announces.

docs.title: Text Content
docs.text: Block-level elements that organise text: headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes and figures.

docs.title: <h1> – <h6> Headings BeginnerHeading 2
docs.text:
Use: section titles, from most important (h1) to least (h6).

<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<h2>Heading 2</h2>
<h3>Heading 3</h3>
<h4>Heading 4</h4>
<h5>Heading 5</h5>
<h6>Heading 6</h6>
Heading 1 Heading 3 Heading 4 Heading 5 Heading 6

Rules:

  • One <h1> per page, describing the page.
  • Don't skip levels (h2 → h4). Screen reader users navigate by heading level and a skip looks like missing content.
  • Pick the level for structure, then use CSS for size. Need a small-looking h2? Style it.

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

About 68% of screen reader users navigate long pages by headings first (WebAIM survey). A correct heading outline is one of the cheapest, highest-impact accessibility wins.

docs.title: <p> Paragraph Beginner
docs.text:
<p>The first paragraph.</p>
<p>The second paragraph, with space above it from the browser's default margin.</p>

The first paragraph.

The second paragraph, with space above it from the browser's default margin.

Common mistake: using empty <p></p> or <br><br> for spacing. Use CSS margin instead.

docs.title: <br> Line break Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a line break that's part of the content, such as in an address or a poem.

<p>221B Baker Street<br>London<br>NW1 6XE</p>

221B Baker StreetLondonNW1 6XE

docs.title: <hr> Thematic break Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a change of topic between paragraphs. It's semantic, not just a line, so screen readers announce it as a separator.

<p>End of chapter one.</p>
<hr>
<p>Chapter two begins.</p>

End of chapter one.

Chapter two begins.

docs.title: <pre> Preformatted text Beginner
docs.text:
Use: keeps whitespace and line breaks exactly as written, in a monospace font. Wrap code in <pre><code>.

<pre><code>function greet() {
  return "hi";
}</code></pre>

function greet() {
  return "hi";
}

docs.title: <blockquote> Block quotation Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a long quote from another source. cite holds the source URL (not shown on screen).

<figure>
  <blockquote cite="https://www.w3.org/standards/webdesign/accessibility">
    <p>The power of the Web is in its universality.</p>
  </blockquote>
  <figcaption>— Tim Berners-Lee</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: <ul> Unordered list Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a list where order doesn't matter. Navigation menus are usually <ul> inside <nav>.

<ul>
  <li>Milk</li>
  <li>Eggs</li>
  <li>Bread</li>
</ul>

docs.title: <ol> Ordered list Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a list where order matters: steps, rankings.

Key attributes: start="5", reversed, type="1 | a | A | i | I". On <li>: value="10".

<ol type="i" start="3">
  <li>Preheat the oven</li>
  <li>Mix the batter</li>
  <li>Bake for 25 minutes</li>
</ol>

<ol reversed>
  <li>Bronze</li>
  <li>Silver</li>
  <li>Gold</li>
</ol>

  2. Mix the batter
  3. Bake for 25 minutes
  1. Bronze
  2. Silver

docs.title: <li> List item Beginner
docs.text:
Use: an item inside <ul>, <ol> or <menu>. Lists can nest: put a whole <ul> inside an <li>.

<ul>
  <li>Frontend
    <ul>
      <li>HTML</li>
      <li>CSS</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Backend</li>
</ul>
  • Frontend
    • HTML
    • CSS
  • Backend

Senior note · 🟠 Advanced

list-style: none makes Safari/VoiceOver stop announcing a list as a list. If the list semantics matter (a nav menu does), add role="list" to the <ul>. Or use list-style-type: "", which hides the bullets and keeps the semantics in current Safari.

docs.title: <dl>, <dt>, <dd> Description list Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: name–value groups: glossaries, metadata, FAQs, key-value specs.

<dl>
  <dt>HTML</dt>
  <dd>Structure and meaning of content.</dd>
  <dt>CSS</dt>
  <dd>Presentation and layout.</dd>
  <dt>JS</dt>
  <dd>Behaviour.</dd>
</dl>
HTML Structure and meaning of content. CSS Presentation and layout. JS Behaviour.

You may wrap each dt/dd group in a <div> for styling (for example, a grid of cards).

docs.title: <div> Generic container Beginner
docs.text:
Use: a block container with no meaning. Use it for styling and layout hooks only, when no semantic element fits.

<div class="card">
  <h3>Plan A</h3>
  <p>For small teams.</p>
</div>
Plan A

For small teams.

docs.title: <figure> and <figcaption> Beginner
docs.text:
Use: self-contained content (image, chart, code, quote) with an optional caption. The figure could be moved to an appendix without breaking the text.

<figure>
  <img src="chart.svg" alt="Revenue grew 40% from Q1 to Q4" width="240" height="120">
  <figcaption>Figure 1: Revenue by quarter, 2026.</figcaption>
</figure>
Figure 1: Revenue by quarter, 2026.

docs.title: <menu> Intermediate
docs.text:
Use: a semantic alternative to <ul> for a list of commands (toolbar buttons). Browsers treat it like <ul>.

<menu>
  <li><button type="button">Copy</button></li>
  <li><button type="button">Cut</button></li>
  <li><button type="button">Paste</button></li>
</menu>
  • Copy
  • Cut
  • Paste

docs.title: <main> Beginner
docs.text: See Sectioning & Landmarks. One visible <main> per page, holding the page's primary content.

docs.title: Layout: Choosing the Right Tool
docs.text:
CSS has four layout systems. Picking the right one is half the job.

flowchart TD
    Q1{"Is it text and simple<br/>blocks stacked top to bottom?"} -- Yes --> F["Normal flow<br/>(no layout CSS needed)"]
    Q1 -- No --> Q2{"Do you control rows AND<br/>columns at the same time?"}
    Q2 -- "Yes (2-D)" --> G["CSS Grid"]
    Q2 -- "No, one direction (1-D)" --> Q3{"Should item sizes come<br/>from their content?"}
    Q3 -- Yes --> FX["Flexbox"]
    Q3 -- "No, strict columns" --> G
    Q1 -- "It overlaps / floats<br/>on top of something" --> P["position: absolute / fixed / sticky<br/>or the top layer (dialog, popover)"]
Flexbox Grid Dimensions 1-D: a row or a column 2-D: rows and columns Sizing comes from Content outward: items decide their size, the container distributes leftovers Layout inward: the container defines tracks, items are placed into them Great for Navbars, toolbars, button groups, centering, media objects, tag lists Page layouts, card grids, dashboards, forms, galleries, overlapping elements Wrapping Each wrapped line is independent (items in row 2 don't align with row 1) Items align to columns across every row

The honest rule of thumb

Use Grid for the overall page and for anything that should line up in columns. Use Flexbox for components inside that grid, and whenever you'd say "put these things in a row and space them out". Most real UIs nest both.

docs.text:
/* A row of 3 equal cards */
.flex { display: flex; gap: 1rem; }
.flex > * { flex: 1; }

.grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 1rem; }

flex-wrap: the last row stretches, columns don't line up

docs.title: Flexbox (complete reference)
docs.text: Flexbox lays items out along one axis. In every demo, the dashed orange box is the flex container and the coloured boxes are flex items.

docs.title: The two axes Beginner
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph "flex-direction: row"
    direction LR
    A[item 1] --> B[item 2] --> C[item 3]
    end
  • Main axis: the direction items flow (row = left→right; column = top→bottom). justify-content works on this axis.
  • Cross axis: perpendicular to it. align-items works on this axis.

When you switch to flex-direction: column, the axes swap, so justify-content becomes vertical.

docs.title: display: flex Beginner
docs.text:
<div class="container">
  <div>1</div><div>2</div><div>3</div>
</div>

.container { display: flex; }
123

Children become flex items: they sit in a row, shrink to fit their content, and stretch to the container's height. display: inline-flex does the same but the container itself flows inline.

docs.title: flex-direction Beginner
docs.text:
flex-direction: row;            /* default */
flex-direction: row-reverse;
flex-direction: column;
flex-direction: column-reverse;
row123 row-reverse123 column123 column-reverse123

Accessibility · 🟠 Advanced

*-reverse and order change only the visual order. Keyboard tab order and screen readers still follow the HTML source order. If the visual and DOM orders disagree, keyboard users see focus jump around. Change the HTML order instead when the order matters.

docs.title: flex-wrap Beginner
docs.text:
flex-wrap: nowrap;        /* default: items shrink, then overflow */
flex-wrap: wrap;          /* items move to new lines */
flex-wrap: wrap-reverse;  /* new lines go above */

(The nowrap demo uses flex-shrink: 0 so you can see the overflow.)

flex-flow: row wrap; is the shorthand for flex-direction + flex-wrap.

docs.title: align-content (multiple lines) Intermediate
docs.text:
Only has an effect when items wrap onto several lines and the container has spare cross-axis space. Same values as justify-content, plus stretch.

.container { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; height: 200px; align-content: space-between; }
stretch (default)1234 flex-start1234 center1234 space-between1234

docs.title: gap Beginner
docs.text:
gap: 1rem;          /* row-gap and column-gap */
gap: 2rem 0.5rem;   /* row-gap column-gap */
12345

Always prefer gap over margins on items: no "remove the margin from the last item" hacks.

docs.title: flex-grow Beginner
docs.text:
How much of the leftover space an item takes, as a proportion.

.a { flex-grow: 0; }   /* default: don't grow */
.b { flex-grow: 1; }   /* takes 1 share */
.c { flex-grow: 2; }   /* takes 2 shares */
grow 0grow 1grow 2

Item 3 gets twice as much of the extra space as item 2. It's not twice as wide overall; the shares are added on top of each item's base size.

docs.title: flex-shrink Intermediate
docs.text:
How much an item gives up when there isn't enough space. Default 1 (all shrink equally, weighted by size). 0 = never shrink.

.logo   { flex-shrink: 0; }   /* never squash the logo */
.title  { flex-shrink: 1; }
shrink 0 (160px)shrink 1shrink 3

docs.title: flex-basis Beginner
docs.text:
The item's starting size before growing or shrinking. auto (default) = use width or content size. 0 = ignore content size, so space is split purely by flex-grow.

flex: 1 1 auto: extra space shared, but long content stays wider AA longer itemB flex: 1 1 0: equal widths regardless of content AA longer itemB

docs.title: flex shorthand Beginner
docs.text:
Always use the shorthand. It sets sensible values for all three.

Shorthand = grow shrink basis Meaning flex: initial 0 1 auto Default. Content-sized, can shrink, won't grow flex: auto 1 1 auto Content-sized, then grows/shrinks flex: none 0 0 auto Rigid: exactly its content/width size flex: 1 1 1 0% Equal share of all space ("make columns equal") flex: 2 2 1 0% Double share flex: 0 0 200px Fixed 200px, never changes flex: 1 1 250px Prefer 250px, wrap when there's no room: the responsive card pattern

Override align-items for one item.

.container { align-items: flex-start; }
.special   { align-self: flex-end; }

Change visual order. Default 0; lower numbers come first. (See the accessibility warning above.)

.first { order: -1; }

docs.title: The min-width: 0 bug Intermediate
docs.text:
Flex items default to min-width: auto, which means they won't shrink below their content's width. A long URL or a white-space: nowrap child will blow out the layout.

.item { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }   /* allow it to shrink; let text-overflow kick in */

.cards { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; }

CardCardCardCard

docs.title: Flexbox interview cheat sheet Advanced
docs.text: Question Answer Difference between justify-content and align-items? Main axis vs cross axis. They swap meaning with flex-direction: column. Why do my flex items overflow instead of shrinking? min-width: auto on flex items. Set min-width: 0 (or overflow: hidden). flex: 1 vs flex: auto? 1 = basis 0, equal widths. auto = basis auto, content-weighted widths. Do margins collapse in flex? No. float on a flex item? Ignored. How does flex-shrink distribute? Proportional to flex-shrink × flex-basis, so big items shrink more. Does vertical-align work? No; use align-items / align-self.

docs.title: CSS Grid (complete reference)
docs.text: Grid lays items out in rows and columns at the same time. In every demo, the dashed orange box is the grid container and the coloured boxes are grid items.

docs.title: Vocabulary Beginner
docs.text: Term Meaning Grid line The dividing lines, numbered from 1 (and from -1 at the end) Track A row or a column (the space between two lines) Cell One row × one column Area A rectangle of one or more cells Gap / gutter Space between tracks Explicit grid Tracks you define with grid-template-* Implicit grid Tracks the browser creates when items don't fit (grid-auto-*)

docs.title: display: grid + columns Beginner
docs.text:
.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 2fr;
  gap: 1rem;
}
120px1fr2fr120px1fr2fr

docs.title: The fr unit Beginner
docs.text:
fr = a fraction of the free space left after fixed tracks and gaps. 1fr 2fr splits leftovers 1:2.

1fr is really minmax(auto, 1fr)

A 1fr column won't shrink below its content's minimum width, the same "won't shrink" behaviour as flex items. If a long word or a wide table blows out your grid, use minmax(0, 1fr).

docs.title: repeat() Beginner
docs.text:
grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);              /* 4 equal columns */
grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 100px 1fr);        /* 100px 1fr 100px 1fr */
grid-template-columns: 250px repeat(3, 1fr);        /* sidebar + 3 equal */
grid-template-columns: repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr));  /* 12-column system */
12345678

docs.title: minmax() Intermediate
docs.text:
grid-template-columns: minmax(150px, 300px) 1fr;  /* first col between 150 and 300px */
grid-auto-rows: minmax(80px, auto);               /* rows at least 80px, grow with content */

docs.title: auto-fill vs auto-fit: responsive with zero media queries Beginner
docs.text:
The single most useful line of CSS layout ("RAM": Repeat, Auto, Minmax):

.cards {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(200px, 100%), 1fr));
  gap: 1rem;
}

"Fit as many columns as possible, each at least 200px, then stretch them to fill the row." The min(200px, 100%) stops overflow on screens narrower than 200px.

auto-fill: keeps empty column slots 12 auto-fit: collapses empty slots, items stretch 12

With few items, auto-fill leaves empty columns and auto-fit stretches the items. With many items, they behave the same.

docs.title: Rows Beginner
docs.text:
grid-template-rows: 80px auto 60px;   /* explicit rows */
grid-auto-rows: 100px;                /* size for any extra (implicit) rows */
grid-auto-rows: minmax(100px, auto);
row 1 (40px)11row 2 (80px)22implicit (30px)33

docs.title: Placing items by line number Beginner
docs.text:
.hero   { grid-column: 1 / 4; }       /* from line 1 to line 4 = 3 columns */
.wide   { grid-column: span 2; }      /* span 2 columns from wherever it lands */
.full   { grid-column: 1 / -1; }      /* first line to last line = full width */
.tall   { grid-row: 1 / 3; }          /* 2 rows */
.box    { grid-area: 2 / 1 / 4 / 3; } /* row-start / col-start / row-end / col-end */
1 / -1 (full width) span 2 rows span 2 cols · · · ·

docs.title: grid-template-areas: draw your layout Beginner
docs.text:
Name areas, then draw the layout as ASCII art. . is an empty cell.

.page {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr;
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;
  grid-template-areas:
    "header header"
    "sidebar main"
    "footer footer";
  min-height: 100dvh;
}
header { grid-area: header; }
aside  { grid-area: sidebar; }
main   { grid-area: main; }
footer { grid-area: footer; }

/* Mobile: just redraw the map */
@media (width < 700px) {
  .page {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
    grid-template-areas: "header" "main" "sidebar" "footer";
  }
}
header sidebar main footer

Rules: every row string must have the same number of cells, and each named area must be a rectangle.

docs.title: Named lines Advanced
docs.text:
.layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns:
    [full-start] minmax(1rem, 1fr)
    [content-start] minmax(0, 60rem) [content-end]
    minmax(1rem, 1fr) [full-end];
}
.layout > *     { grid-column: content; }   /* centred content column */
.layout > .full { grid-column: full; }      /* full-bleed images, banners */

This "full-bleed" layout is covered in Layout Patterns.

docs.title: Implicit grid and grid-auto-flow Intermediate
docs.text:
grid-auto-flow: row;          /* default: fill row by row */
grid-auto-flow: column;       /* fill column by column */
grid-auto-flow: row dense;    /* backfill holes with later small items */

The one-line centre Beginner

.center { display: grid; place-items: center; }
Centered with 2 properties

docs.title: Overlapping items Intermediate
docs.text:
Grid lets several items occupy the same cell: an alternative to position: absolute that keeps everything in flow.

.hero { display: grid; }
.hero > * { grid-area: 1 / 1; }        /* everything in the same cell */
.hero .text { place-self: end start; z-index: 1; }
Text stacked on the image, no absolute positioning

docs.title: Subgrid Advanced
docs.text: See Modern CSS → Subgrid for a live demo. grid-template-columns: subgrid or grid-template-rows: subgrid lets nested elements align to the parent grid's tracks.

docs.title: Masonry Expert
docs.text: A native masonry layout (Pinterest-style) is being standardised as CSS Grid Lanes (display: grid-lanes), with an earlier experimental syntax grid-template-rows: masonry in Firefox and Safari Technology Preview. It isn't Baseline yet. Until it is, use CSS multi-column (columns: 3 220px, ordered top-to-bottom per column) or a JS library. See Layout Patterns → Masonry.

docs.title: Grid cheat sheet Advanced
docs.text: You want Write N equal columns grid-template-columns: repeat(N, 1fr) Responsive cards repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(250px, 100%), 1fr)) Sidebar + content grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr (or minmax(200px, 25%) 1fr) Full width item grid-column: 1 / -1 Centre one thing display: grid; place-items: center Stack things on top of each other grid-area: 1 / 1 on every child Columns that don't blow out minmax(0, 1fr) instead of 1fr Equal-height rows of cards grid-auto-rows: 1fr Fill gaps from wide items grid-auto-flow: dense (watch out for reading order)

docs.title: Layout Patterns
docs.text:
Real-world layouts you'll build again and again. Each has the code and a live, responsive output. Most demos react to your browser width; resize to see them adapt.

All of them, plus extra ones, are also on the standalone Layout Gallery page.

docs.title: 1. Centering: six ways
docs.text:
Beginner

/* 1. Grid: the shortest */
.a { display: grid; place-items: center; }

/* 2. Flexbox */
.b { display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; }

/* 3. Flex/grid parent + margin auto on the child */
.c { display: flex; }  .c > * { margin: auto; }

/* 4. Absolute + translate (works anywhere, e.g. over an image) */
.d { position: relative; }  .d > * { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; translate: -50% -50%; }

/* 5. Absolute + inset + margin auto (child needs a size) */
.e > * { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: fit-content; height: fit-content; }

/* 6. Horizontal only: a block with a width */
.f > * { max-width: 40rem; margin-inline: auto; }

/* Text only */
.g { text-align: center; }

docs.title: 2. Holy grail layout
docs.text:
Beginner Header, footer, main content between two sidebars. Stacks on mobile.

<div class="holy">
  <header>Header</header>
  <nav>Nav</nav>
  <main>Main</main>
  <aside>Aside</aside>
  <footer>Footer</footer>
</div>

.holy {
  display: grid;
  gap: 1rem;
  grid-template: auto 1fr auto / 1fr;        /* rows / columns */
  grid-template-areas: "header" "nav" "main" "aside" "footer";
  min-height: 100dvh;
}
@media (width >= 48em) {
  .holy {
    grid-template-columns: 180px 1fr 180px;
    grid-template-areas:
      "header header header"
      "nav    main   aside"
      "footer footer footer";
  }
}
.holy > header { grid-area: header; }
.holy > nav    { grid-area: nav; }
.holy > main   { grid-area: main; }
.holy > aside  { grid-area: aside; }
.holy > footer { grid-area: footer; }

docs.text:
Intermediate The sidebar sits beside the content when there's room and wraps above it when there isn't.

.with-sidebar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; }
.with-sidebar > :first-child { flex: 1 1 200px; }          /* sidebar: ideal 200px */
.with-sidebar > :last-child  { flex: 999 1 0; min-inline-size: 60%; }  /* content takes the rest; wraps under 60% */

docs.text:
Beginner Header and footer take their natural height; main fills the rest, so the footer is always at the bottom even on short pages.

body { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto; min-height: 100dvh; }

Advanced Readable text column, with some elements (images, quotes) breaking out to the full width.

.article {

.auto:has(> :nth-child(2)) { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
